§9.5.2 Nested Tables

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-nested-tables · tables encoding rare

✅ Normative

A small grid printed inside one cell of a table MUST be rendered by subdividing that cell into the outer table's own grid: the inner grid's cells become rows and columns of the outer table, and the neighbouring cells span them. The output MUST NOT contain a nested <table> element, and MUST NOT flatten the inner grid into text.

A cell that itself contains a small grid: a fee schedule inside a plan-comparison cell, a mini-table of components inside one row of a summary.

| Plan | Fees                          |
| A    | ┌ admin │ 0.25% ┐            |
|      | └ fund  │ 0.10% ┘   ← a table inside the cell

Recognising a nested table

The inner grid has its own alignment: two or more columns of its own, sometimes its own header row, and its own row boundaries that do not line up with the outer table's rows. That is what separates it from a cell that merely holds several lines of text, which is governed by Record Groups and Multi-Line Cells§9.5.3.

Rendering

The inner grid's cells MUST become real cells of the outer table, and every cell alongside it MUST span the rows it now occupies:

<tr>
  <td rowspan="2">A</td>
  <td>admin</td><td>0.25%</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td>fund</td><td>0.10%</td>
</tr>

A is printed once and genuinely covers both fee rows, so rowspan="2" is a true statement about the page — the same test Repeated Identical Values§9.5.4 applies everywhere else.

  • No nested <table>. A nested table makes the inner grid invisible to anything that walks the outer one: cell counts, column arithmetic and per-cell boxes all stop at the <td> boundary. Subdividing keeps every value addressable at the same level as the rest of the table, and the outer grid still reconciles — see the leaf-track check in Multi-Row Header Tiers§9.3.3.
  • Pairs MUST survive. The pairing inside the inner grid is the data: admin goes with 0.25% and fund with 0.10%. An encoding that lists all the labels and then all the values has destroyed the table; so has flattening the cell to <br/>-separated text.

This is one of several cases that need HTML tables rather than pipe tables, which cannot express the spans this rule depends on (see Markdown Rendering§3.2). The others are spans in Multi-Row Header Tiers§9.3.3, full-width band rows in Bands Inside the Grid§9.2.1, and level markers on the stub in Row-Label Hierarchy§9.5.5.

✅ Sample — en

The left two columns form an embedded Section / Marks mini-table, with its own Summative Assessment II / 30% heading row, while a single ruled cell on the right spans all five of its rows and prints nothing. The TOTAL row is bold.

  <tr> <th colspan="2">Division of Syllabus for Term II (October-March)</th> <th>Total Weightage Assigned</th> </tr>

</table>

✅ Sample — korean-curriculum

A rowspan-6 단 원 별 교 육 내 용 stub encloses its own mini-grid — complete with a shaded header row 단원(제목) / 시수 / 교육내용 — inside the outer table. The shaded label cells on the left are bold; the two bulleted cells print • bullets.
